Senses.PreferredTarget: a day without work is a day without food
AlternateTargets: if I do not work for a day, I do not eat for a day
Senses.Explanation: Literally, “one day not working, one day not eating.” The Chan institutional record attributes the saying to Baizhang and ties it to shared manual labor: the monastic regulations say that even in old age he “shared the community's labor” (與眾均其勞) and regularly said the line. The same regulations later call it “the warning of the ancients” (古人之誡) when directing the community to attend communal work. Xutang's record adds that at age ninety-five Baizhang's hoe, cutting tool, rain cape, and bamboo hat never left him. Hongzhi quotes the saying and calls “farming to obtain food to eat” (種田博飯喫) “the house style” (家風). Its Zen deviation is institutional and explicit: a maxim attached to Baizhang becomes the recorded house rule for the teacher's and community's agricultural labor.
Senses.Note: The exact saying occurs 8 times in 6 allowlisted texts. Independent witnesses preserve attribution to Baizhang, its later status as an injunction for communal labor, and Hongzhi's house-style quotation. No competing wording establishes a separate sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 至於作務。猶與眾均其勞。常曰。一日不作一日不食。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 勅修百丈清規. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Baizhang Huaihai as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 並宜齊赴。當思古人一日不作一日不食之誡。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 勅修百丈清規. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Dehui as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日不作一日不食。歇者無心穫者力。分明只箇是家風。會得種田博飯喫。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄), in Hongzhi Zhengjue's hall address: Hongzhi Zhengjue states the maxim ‘A day without work is a day without food,’ calls it ‘the house style,’ and follows it with ‘farming to obtain food to eat.’
